chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him) said:

I wrote to him regarding a man who died, and he had an umm al-walad (concubine who bore a child), and he had allocated something for her during his lifetime, then he died. He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'For her is what her master remunerated to her during his lifetime in goodness, that is for her. The testimony of the man, and the woman, and the servant not having been accused of any wrong, would be acceptable upon that'.

key_terms.أَثَابَهَا: He remunerated/rewarded her: Refers to the provision or bequest given.
key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Umm al-walad: A concubine who bore a child to her master, gaining specific status in Islamic law.
key_terms.الْخَادِمِ: The servant: A domestic servant whose testimony is also accepted in this context.
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ الرَّجُلِ وَ الْمَرْأَةِ: Testimony of a man and a woman: A specific combination of witnesses accepted for verifying this ruling.
key_terms.غَيْرِ الْمُتَّهَمِينَ: Not accused/suspected: Witnesses who are free from bias or suspicion of partiality.
key_terms.مَعْرُوفٌ: Goodness/Standard: Refers to a reasonable or customary amount as determined by the master.

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance right of an umm al-walad if her master made a specific bequest for her during his lifetime?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the posthumous rights of an umm al-walad, affirming that her bequest is binding and enforceable via the testimony of one man, one woman, and one servant, reflecting the practical application of inheritance law in early Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the flexibility in evidentiary standards for such claims, ensuring the woman's status and financial security are protected according to the master's explicit intent. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on honoring the master's voluntary allocation while maintaining social justice for the mother of his child.

en.hubeali:
Ahamd Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Khalid Al Sayrafi,
(It has been narrated) from Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) said, ‘

I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who died, and for whom was a mother of a child, and he had made something to be for her during his lifetime, then died’. He<sup>asws</sup> said by writing: ‘For her is what her master remunerated to her during his lifetime in goodness, that is for her. The testimony of the man, and the woman, and the servant not having been accused of any wrong, would be acceptable upon that’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Husayn ibn Khalid who has narrated the following: “I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, before this abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who died and left behind a mother of child for whom he willed something in his lifetime, then died. He (the Imam) wrote, ‘She can have what her master had given her in his lifetime in an acceptable manner. The testimony of both man and woman is acceptable in it as well as the testimony of a servant who is not accused of wrong doing.’”
